summary.intent: Determine whether the changesets written by workers across open PR branches are user-friendly and user-forward, and whether their headings and bullets are appropriate for how they will appear in the future changelog.
summary.outcome: Partially completed audit: identified the repo's changeset convention and found only 12 changesets across about 37 open branches, then began reading bodies and the changelog format. No final assessment of style compliance or any fixes had been produced by the end of the transcript.

repo: Repo rule for changesets: one short consumer-facing paragraph, outcome first, no heading or list marker at the start, no hard wrapping.
Changeset writing guidance and examples live on main and can be found via the repo's changeset conventions.
Only 12 changesets exist across roughly 37 open PR branches, so many user-visible fixes have no changeset at all.
Changeset bodies are rendered into a generated changelog, so heading and bullet use in a changeset affects changelog structure; a callisto config also governs the changelog format.
workflow: Check the repo's own written conventions and examples on main before judging worker output, rather than relying on general style assumptions.
Audit changesets across all open PR branches in one pass, then read bodies alongside the generated changelog format to judge how they will render.

friction: The assistant had not reviewed the changesets against any style guide before the question, so the audit had to start from scratch.
The working directory is not a git repository, so repo inspection relied on Bash commands against other locations.
open_items: Finish evaluating the 12 changesets against the one-paragraph, outcome-first, no-heading/list rule and report violations.
Decide whether to add changesets for the many branches with user-visible fixes that have none.
Rewrite any non-compliant changesets so they render cleanly in the changelog.
